research_rationale: Executive Order 11294 of August 4, 1966 (31 FR 10601) has four sections, all read in the held Federal Register text: section 1 amends Executive Order 10621 by adding paragraph (o) (the President's authority under section 3 of the Travel Expense Act of 1949 to set maximum per diem rates in Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico, the Canal Zone and possessions, delegated to the Secretary of Defense); section 2 delegates to the Secretary of State the same authority for areas outside the United States; section 3 amends paragraph (9) of Section 1 of Executive Order 11230 (the same authority for travel to and between places outside the 48 contiguous States, delegated to the Director of the Bureau of the Budget); and section 4 supersedes Executive Order 10970, to the extent not heretofore superseded. Two later orders act on it. Executive Order 11609 of July 22, 1971, section 11, lists among the orders hereby superseded Section 3 of Executive Order No. 11294 of August 4, 1966 (together with Executive Order 11230 that it amended); section 12 makes the order effective immediately except paragraphs (1) to (13) and (19) of its section 1, so the supersession of section 3 took effect on July 22, 1971 (the machine lead of October 20, 1971 is the ninety-day date for those paragraphs of section 1, which does not include section 11). Executive Order 12561 of July 1, 1986 (51 FR 24299), section 1 revokes subsection (o) of Section 1 of EO 10621 (the paragraph section 1 of EO 11294 added), section 2 re-delegates the per diem authority to the Secretary of State under section 102(a) of the Federal Civilian Employee and Contractor Travel Expenses Act of 1985, and section 3 states that Executive Order No. 11294 of August 4, 1966, is revoked. That express revocation of the whole order on July 1, 1986 ends sections 1, 2 and 4, and is the latest clause end, so the whole order ended on July 1, 1986. Executive Order 12396 of December 9, 1982 revoked subsections (g), (h), (j), (k), (l), (m) and (n) of Section 1 of EO 10621 but not subsection (o), so it did not end section 1. The held U.S. Code note under 3 U.S.C. 301 (jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t3-s301.txt) agrees: it says EO 11294, as amended by EO 11609, was revoked by EO 12561. The Federal Register disposition note held for EO 11294 gives EO 10960 of October 27, 1961 as the order superseded, but the order's text (and EO 10970 of October 27, 1961) says 10970; the text controls. The machine lead naming EO 11488 is an unrelated land order that does not cite EO 11294 and is disregarded. Status recommended: no.
savings_reason: The delegated per diem authority did not lapse: Executive Order 12561 of July 1, 1986 re-delegated it in sections 1 and 2 under the 1985 Act, so the function continues under that order's own authority, and the supersession of EO 10970 in section 4 and the earlier amendments of EO 10621 and EO 11230 are accrued effects that no longer depend on EO 11294. EO 11294 contains no savings clause.
earlier_end_check: Earlier partial end: section 3 was superseded by section 11 of EO 11609 on July 22, 1971 (the section 12 delayed paragraphs do not include section 11). No instrument is held that ends sections 1, 2 or 4 before the revocation by EO 12561 of July 1, 1986; EO 12396 (December 9, 1982) revoked other subsections of EO 10621 but not subsection (o), and EO 11609 names only section 3 of EO 11294.
scope_check: Four clauses were checked separately: EO 11609 reaches only section 3; EO 12561 revokes the whole order and also revokes subsection (o) of EO 10621 (the effect of section 1) and re-delegates the section 2 function; the inventory of four sections is complete for the held text of the order.
independent_command_check: Section 4 (supersession of EO 10970) is a one-time command that took effect on issue; sections 1 and 3 are amending instructions whose effect lives in the parent orders EO 10621 and EO 11230 and who end with the parent paragraph or the amending order; section 2 is the only freestanding delegation. No section is independent of these dates, and none survives the express revocation of the whole order.
savings_check: Savings state transferred_or_accrued: the per diem function continues under EO 12561 and the 1985 Act; EO 11294 has no savings clause.

research_rationale: Executive Order 13476 of October 9, 2008 (Facilitation of a Presidential Transition, 73 FR 60605, printed October 14, 2008) establishes a Presidential Transition Coordinating Council, directs transition activities and materials, and provides for transition agreements, all for the 2008 presidential transition. Section 4(d) fixes its own end: unless extended by the President, the order expires on February 20, 2009. The held registered text of the whole order was read; every operative clause is therefore time-limited by section 4(d), and the order's own terms end all of its clauses on that date. No extension is held: the bounded searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) and a search of the held order texts for the order's number found no later instrument that extends, amends or revokes it; the one catalog hit is the Federal Register note citing EO 13467 of June 30, 2008 (it also records that this order supersedes EO 13176), a cross-reference to the order that created the Suitability and Security Clearance Performance Accountability Council mentioned in section 2(c), not an ending or amendment of this order. Section 4(a) supersedes Executive Order 13176 of November 27, 2000; that supersession took effect on issue and is an accrued effect, not a continuing command. The whole-order end is February 20, 2009, recorded inclusive as the stated date (the exclusive reading, under which the order ended when that day began, is the alternative). Status recommended: no. The inventory is the machine segmentation of the order (31 scopes); it covers the text from section 1 through section 4(d), with section 1(a) split at an internal citation fragment and the lettered and numbered items of sections 1(b) and 4(b) listed as separate scopes, and no operative text is outside it.
savings_reason: The order states that it creates no right or benefit enforceable at law (section 4(c)) and confers no function independent of the Council it established. Transition agreements and Council activities were performed for the 2008-2009 transition; nothing in the held text or in the bounded searches shows any right, duty or program of this order continuing after its expiry on February 20, 2009. The Presidential Transition Act and the later transition orders are separate bases, not continuations of this order.
earlier_end_check: No revocation, supersession or amendment of EO 13476 earlier than its own expiry date is held: the OFR catalog hit is only a cross-reference to EO 13467, the U.S. Code and eCFR searches found no citation of the order, and no held text cites the order's number other than its own two printings. Its own section 4(d) expiry date (February 20, 2009) is therefore the first end.
scope_check: All 31 inventoried scopes (sections 1 through 4(d), including the nested officer lists and section 4(b) items) fall under the order-wide time limit in section 4(d); section 4(a) (the supersession of EO 13176) takes effect on issue but is recorded as ending with the order, as the only held ending source is the order's own expiry; no clause is partly continuing or stated to survive expiry.
independent_command_check: The order contains no command independent of the time limit: the Council, the departmental support duties in section 2 and the transition agreements in section 3 all exist only for the 2008-2009 transition and end with the order. Section 4(a) supersedes EO 13176, a performed command, and section 4(b) and 4(c) are non-command construction clauses.
savings_check: Savings state none_after_bounded_search: section 4(c) disclaims any enforceable right, and the held texts and bounded searches show no surviving right or duty.

research_rationale: Executive Order 12437 of August 11, 1983 (Fuel Use Prohibitions, 48 FR 36801) is a single paragraph whose only command is that "Executive Order No. 12217 is revoked." It creates no continuing duty, office, standard or deadline. A command that revokes another order is carried out when the order issues, so the order's own operative force was spent on issue (signing date August 11, 1983; filed for publication 8-12-83, printed August 15, 1983). Status recommended: no. The only clause is therefore terminated on 1983-08-11 by performance of its own terms. The consequence that survives, EO 12217 remaining revoked, is an accrued effect of the revocation and is not a continuing command of EO 12437. The Federal Register disposition note held for this order records that it revokes EO 12217 of June 18, 1980, and the held U.S. Code text at jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t42-s8373.txt recites that EO 12217 was revoked by this order; both recite the revocation and neither amends or ends EO 12437. The bounded searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog found no later instrument that amends, supersedes or revokes EO 12437, and a search of the held texts for its number found no citation in any other held text. No later event is claimed.
savings_reason: The only legal consequence that survives is that Executive Order No. 12217 stands revoked. That is an accrued effect of the revocation carried out on issue; nothing in the order's text reserves, saves or continues any right, duty or program of EO 12437 itself, and the order contains no savings clause.
earlier_end_check: No instrument earlier than the signing date can have ended an order issued on August 11, 1983; the order's own sole command was performed on issue, and no held source shows an earlier or later revocation, supersession or amendment of EO 12437.
scope_check: The order is one paragraph with one operative sentence and no section division; the inventory has one clause, the whole order, covering the revocation of EO 12217. The order text read in full contains nothing else operative.
independent_command_check: There is no separate standing command, delegation, reporting duty or office in the order apart from the revocation sentence; the purpose recital about administrative burdens under the Powerplant and Industrial Fuel Use Act of 1978 states why EO 12217 is revoked and commands nothing.
savings_check: Savings state transferred_or_accrued: EO 12217 remains revoked as an accrued result of performance; no savings clause exists in EO 12437.

research_rationale: Executive Order 12753 of March 8, 1991 (Nuclear Cooperation With EURATOM, 56 FR 10501) is one paragraph. Under section 126a(2) of the Atomic Energy Act of 1954 (42 U.S.C. 2155(a)(2)) it determines that failure to continue nuclear cooperation with the European Atomic Energy Community would be seriously prejudicial to U.S. non-proliferation objectives, extends the duration of the statutory period to March 10, 1992, and provides that Executive Order No. 12706 shall be superseded on the effective date of the order. It is a one-year extension in a yearly series. Its own terms limit it to March 10, 1992. Executive Order 12791 of March 9, 1992 (57 FR 8717), the next link in the series (quoted from its American Presidency Project capture, a mirror transcription cited under the transcription ruling; the Federal Register text held in jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_12791.txt has the same sentence), says that Executive Order No. 12753 shall be superseded on the effective date of that order, extends the period to March 10, 1993, and so replaced EO 12753 before or at the end of its own period. EO 12791 states no separate effective date, so its signing date, March 9, 1992, is used as the first end (the Federal Register disposition note held for this order likewise records that it was superseded by EO 12791 of March 9, 1992); the alternative reading is the order's own stated end of the period on March 10, 1992, one day later, which cannot make the first end later than that. Either way the order had no force by March 11, 1992, and nothing in the held sources shows any later revival. The U.S. Code, eCFR and OFR catalog searches found no citation or action that continues EO 12753. Status recommended: no. The one-clause inventory is complete for this one-paragraph order.
savings_reason: The determination and extension concerned the period ending March 10, 1992; cooperation carried out during that period is an accrued effect, and the function of extending the period continued only through the successor orders in the series (EO 12791 of March 9, 1992 and its successors), each making its own determination. The order states no savings clause and no right or duty of EO 12753 itself continued.
earlier_end_check: No instrument earlier than EO 12791 is held that revokes or supersedes EO 12753; the Federal Register disposition note held for it records only that it supersedes EO 12706 and is superseded by EO 12791, and the held order texts that cite its number are the recitals in EO 12791 (and the later orders in the series). EO 12791's supersession (March 9, 1992, effective date not separately stated) precedes or coincides with the order's own end of period (March 10, 1992).
scope_check: The order is a single paragraph with one clause covering the determination, the extension to March 10, 1992 and the supersession of EO 12706; there is no partial supersession: EO 12791 supersedes EO 12753 without limiting words.
independent_command_check: There is no command in EO 12753 independent of the extension period: the sentence that EO 12706 shall be superseded on the effective date of this order is a one-time command spent when EO 12753 took effect, and the recital of earlier orders in the series commands nothing.
savings_check: Savings state transferred_or_accrued: cooperation under the March 1991 to March 1992 period is accrued and the function passed to the successor extension orders; no savings clause in the order.
